payload.feature:
STORY UNIT 1212b FOR ISSUE #1212 (DECISION 0109 SLICE 0109a1'S FOLLOW-UP): PLAIN `inspect`'S VERDICTS WINDOW READS ONLY THE ENGINE'S TWO MARKERS, FILTERED IN SQL ON THE STORED CHECKPOINT BEFORE ANY ENVELOPE IS DECODED, SO ITS COST NO LONGER GROWS WITH EVERY SEAT TURN IN THE WINDOW.

The branch is story-1212b-marker-prefilter, checked out in this worktree at origin/main 52503babf. It is on main: 0109a1 merged there as #1216 (335935931). When you are done, the branch is 52503babf plus your commits. Do not rebase, squash, amend or merge main: the controller restacks.

THE UNIT. Read #1212 whole, in particular c-7061670779 (this item) and c-7060358484 (the by-hand R1/R3 fix). Also read #1216 c-7061668662 (the Callgrind ruling): main's `inspect fixture_run` is +14.0% over its pre-0109a1 base (23.8M to 27.2M instructions). That cost is accepted as the verdicts block's own, and this unit is the recommended cut.

WHERE IT STANDS (correct this where it is wrong):
- crates/brokkr-cli/src/verbs/readouts.rs `verdict_rows` (about :260-290) reads every checkpoint in (head−1000, head] through `Store::envelopes_of_checkpoints` (brokkr-store read.rs, `CHECKPOINTS_BETWEEN`), and decodes each envelope. Then it reads the window's verdict attempts' member markers through `Store::envelopes_of_member_markers` (`MEMBER_MARKERS`).
- Only two kinds of checkpoint carry a verdict or mark one:
  - the engine's authored `sequence-step-finished`, a step record whose result is a verdict;
  - the engine's authored `panel-member-finished`, a member's mark.
  Every other checkpoint (seat turns, telemetry, a driver's record of either word) is read and decoded for nothing. On the Callgrind fixture, 88 of 105 rows are checkpoints, and none is a marker.
- `MEMBER_MARKERS` already filters on the stored checkpoint in SQL: the payload's LAST `checkpoint` key, read as the index projection reads it, then its `step` and `authored`. `EngineMarker::{StepFinished, MemberFinished}.record` writes both fields (brokkr-core findings/marker.rs). 117395b3b holds the store test's copy of the words to `EngineMarker` by building its rows through `record`.

THE OPERATOR'S RULING: the standing ruling of 2026-11-04 ("go with recommended on anything else that comes up", "and by hand") covers this unit and its brokkr-store API change. It never covers accepting a security risk. The controller records each recommendation taken on #1212.

THE WORK (one commit per item, each with its tests and a removal control recorded in the commit message; if your attempt is killed, read `git log` first and do not redo a committed item):

**1. The window reads only the engine's markers.**
- Replace the window's checkpoint read with `Store::envelopes_of_engine_markers(run_id, from, to)`: the run's checkpoints in `from..=to` whose stored checkpoint is an engine marker. That is `step` in {`sequence-step-finished`, `panel-member-finished`} and `authored = 'engine'`, read as `MEMBER_MARKERS` reads them, before any envelope is decoded, in seq order.
- **Give the SQL fragment one home.** `MEMBER_MARKERS` and the new statement share one builder for the stored checkpoint's last-key read and its `step`/`authored` texts, so the two cannot drift.
- `verdict_rows` uses it, and `envelopes_of_checkpoints` is removed if nothing else reads it (it has no other production caller on main today). Name the API lines either way.
- Everything else holds exactly:
  - the elision line, and its count of rows left unread;
  - X6's head bound and V5's repaired tail (`records` filters on the fold);
  - a verdict whose attempt began before the window;
  - a member finish before the window, read as context;
  - `--json`, `--phase` and `--seat` reading whole;
  - an index-less journal reading whole.
- **Tests:**
  - **the store:** a window holding a seat turn, a driver's checkpoint naming each word without `authored`, the engine's step record and member marker (both written through `EngineMarker::*.record`), and a row outside the window. Only the two engine rows inside the window come back, in seq order;
  - **inspect:** every existing readouts and verdict-window test passes unchanged;
  - **a query-plan check,** in the style of seat_read/tests.rs (about :490): the new statement searches by the run's primary-key range or a named index, never a scan of other runs.
  - **Removal control:** drop the `step` filter, and the store test reads the seat turn.

**2. Measure it.** CI's Callgrind on the PR measures `inspect fixture_run` against main, and the controller reads it. Locally:
- report the fixture's row and checkpoint counts and how many envelopes the window now decodes;
- don't claim a Callgrind number you didn't measure; valgrind is on neither host.

FILES EXPECTED: crates/brokkr-store/src/read.rs and its tests (event_index/tests.rs); crates/brokkr-cli/src/verbs/readouts.rs and readouts/tests.rs where a test must move; quality/public-api/brokkr-store.txt.

NOT: brokkr-core (findings/ is decision 0109's, and 0109a2 is changing it now), bundle/, engine/, brokkr-view's residual_findings.rs, any contract, charter or recipe. If the work seems to need any of them, stop and say why.

GATES:
- cargo fmt --all -- --check
- cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
- cargo test -p brokkr-store --lib --locked (timeout 900); cargo test -p brokkr-cli --lib --locked (timeout 1500); cargo test -p brokkr-cli --locked --test it -- gate_readouts readouts inspect (timeout 900)
- typos --hidden; quality/ratchet.sh files, clones and api; git diff --check
- **THE SHARED JOURNAL.** Never point a binary built from this branch, through any verb, at ~/source/feedback-loop-ai/the-forge/.forge/forge.db or any worktree's .forge/forge.db. Lanes run queue storage v5, and main is v6. Every test uses its own temporary journal.
- Each production function keeps cyclomatic complexity at 15 or below, and every `?` counts one. Production files stay at or under 800 lines, and test files under 2,000.
- **The commit:** "<area>: … (#1212, decision 0109 slice 0109a1 follow-up)", signed off.
- Before reporting, `git status --short` shows no untracked file.

THEN: the review panel reviews the whole unit, 52503babf to your head. It checks each of the following and reports each as a test case:
- that no verdict a plain inspect showed before is lost, across a step record, a member's settled payload, a member finish before the window, a repaired tail, and a row appended after the frame;
- that a driver's checkpoint naming either word is never read as the engine's;
- the SQL's one home;
- the query plan.
Each position reports findings with their severity and evidence, and does not state a verdict. The chief decides the outcome.

ASKS TO NAME (for the PR): the API lines; the decoded-envelope count on the fixture.

CONTENTION: code. NEVER message the-forge-98, the-forge-a6 or any brokkr-wt-* seat.

# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.

instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `recipes/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

result.notes: Item 1 is committed as 1c7b730ac (signed G, signed off), on top of 52503babf with no rebase. New Store::envelopes_of_engine_markers(run_id, from, to) (statement ENGINE_MARKERS in brokkr-store read.rs): it returns the run's checkpoints in from..=to whose stored checkpoint (the payload's last `checkpoint`, read as the index projection reads it) has step in {sequence-step-finished, panel-member-finished} and authored='engine', in seq order. The filter runs in SQL before any envelope is decoded. SQL one home: a new builder, engine_marker(event, steps), holds the last-checkpoint read, the step/authored texts and the two words (STEP_FINISHED, MEMBER_FINISHED). MEMBER_MARKERS now calls it too. verdict_rows in readouts.rs calls the new read. envelopes_of_checkpoints and CHECKPOINTS_BETWEEN are removed because nothing else read them (grep showed readouts.rs:272 was the only caller). API LINES: '- pub fn brokkr_store::Store::envelopes_of_checkpoints(&self, &str, u64, u64) -> ...' and '+ pub fn brokkr_store::Store::envelopes_of_engine_markers(&self, &str, u64, u64) -> ...'. quality/ratchet.sh api reports 'public API holds'. TESTS: a_verdict_window_reads_only_the_engine_s_markers_inside_it (event_index/tests.rs) replaces a_checkpoint_window_reads_only_its_checkpoints. Its rows: an engine step record before the window, a seat turn stamped authored=engine, a driver's checkpoint naming each word without authored, a MemberFinished.record marker, a non-checkpoint, a StepFinished.record marker, and a marker after the window. Only [5, 7] come back. the_engine_markers_search_the_run_s_key_range (read/tests.rs) is the plan check on the 105-row fixture: the top-level steps are 'SEARCH i USING PRIMARY KEY (run_id=? AND seq>? AND seq<?)', 'SEARCH e USING INDEX sqlite_autoindex_events_1 (run_id=? AND seq=?)' and two correlated subqueries (the checkpoint walk), with no top-level sort. Assumption: the framing's removal control (drop the step filter, the test reads the seat turn) can only fail if the seat turn also carries authored=engine, because the authored filter alone would still drop it. So the test's seat turn carries authored=engine; it stands for an engine-authored non-marker checkpoint. REMOVAL CONTROLS, each run and restored: step filter dropped -> window test left [2, 5, 7] (and the member-marker test left [1, 4, 6]); authored filter dropped -> [3, 4, 5, 7]; '+i.run_id' -> plan test saw 'SCAN i USING' plus 'USE TEMP B-TREE'. A first try with 'OR 0' was folded away by SQLite and the test passed, so that mutation was not a valid control. MEASURE (scratch assertion, removed before commit): the Callgrind fixture tui-graph-the-selection-box-gets-80f98deb (the same RUN as benches/budgets_bin.rs) has 105 rows, 88 checkpoints and 0 engine markers. The window (cut=0) now decodes 0 envelopes, against 88 before, and the member-marker read does not run there. Callgrind was not measured: valgrind is not on the host, so CI's number is pending. GATES run: cargo fmt --check clean; clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -D warnings clean; cargo test -p brokkr-store --lib 695 passed; cargo test -p brokkr-cli --lib 1484 passed, 2 ignored; --test it gate_readouts/readouts/inspect 33 passed (the existing readouts and verdict-window tests are unchanged); typos --hidden clean; ratchet files/clones/api hold; git diff --check clean; git status --short is empty. Not run: cargo test --workspace in full, the recipes/self compile, and the exact-coverage gate (it must run outside the box; pending). Files touched: read.rs, read/tests.rs, event_index/tests.rs, readouts.rs (doc and call only), and quality/public-api/brokkr-store.txt. read/tests.rs is the read module's own test file, beside the event_index/tests.rs the framing names; it holds the plan test because ENGINE_MARKERS is private to read.rs.

members.adversarial: Adversarial review of 52503babf..1c7b730ac (one commit, branch story-1212b-marker-prefilter, clean status). Four checks. (1) NO VERDICT LOST: brokkr-view's gate_records_within/records/verdicts_of/settled_marks/site_members read checkpoints only where EngineMarker::authored is StepFinished or MemberFinished (residual_findings.rs:98,232,277,320); every other verdict source (effect/succeeded, failed/indeterminate settled_members, effect requested/started context) is a non-checkpoint trail row, untouched. ENGINE_MARKERS' step+authored filter drops only rows the view ignores. I checked the SQL's last-copy semantics against a scratch SQLite 3.46: duplicate checkpoint keys and duplicate step/authored keys resolve last-wins exactly as serde does, and the i.type clause excludes a non-checkpoint carrying a marker-shaped checkpoint; the only divergence I could build (duplicate top-level payload keys) is refused by EventEnvelope's derived duplicate-field check, so it never reaches this read.
